coordinates.locator: geometry:canfranc-lab-underground (OpenStreetMap-georeferenced underground laboratory point, accuracy 150 m)
coordinates.note: Point for the underground laboratory between the Somport tunnels, georeferenced from OpenStreetMap; it is shown as approximate because an OpenStreetMap tracing is not a survey. It replaces the laboratory's administrative building at Canfranc-Estación, 3.0 km from the underground halls.

depth.quote: It has a depth of 800 m under Mount Tobazo.

depth_mwe.note: Hall B of the new laboratory, per the ANAIS-112 collaboration; the muon flux was measured in Hall A. Pandola 2011 gives "about 2400 m w.e." as the maximum rock overburden of the new laboratory. The laboratory's own pages give 800 m of rock and no water-equivalent figure.
depth_mwe.quote: The hut housing the experiment is at the hall B of LSC under 2450 m.w.e.

muon_flux.locator: Abstract and Sec. 3, Eur. Phys. J. C 79 (2019) 721 (arXiv:1902.00868)
muon_flux.note: Hall A of the LAB2400, measured with a dedicated Muon Monitor (three layers of scintillator, 352 pixels, flux-defining area 1 m^2, all azimuth angles and zenith angles up to 80 degrees); statistical uncertainty about 0.2%, dominant systematic ±4%. The paper reports (4.29 ± 0.17) × 10^-3 m^-2 s^-1 for its other location, LAB2500, and says these values supersede preliminary ones that were 20% too low for LAB2400. Pandola 2011 quotes a residual muon flux of 2 to 4 × 10^-3 m^-2 s^-1 depending on the location.
muon_flux.quote: The measured integrated muon flux is (5.26 ± 0.21) × 10−3 m−2 s−1 in the Hall A of the LAB2400

summary.plain: An underground physics laboratory under Mount Tobazo in the Spanish Pyrenees, reached via a former railway tunnel near the village of Canfranc.
summary.technical: Underground hall beneath Mount Tobazo, Canfranc-Estacion, Huesca, at ~800 m depth, excavated from the disused Somport (Canfranc) railway tunnel near the France-Spain border.
